_review.how: Blind to condition and outcome, from contamination_review.py's output, plus scripted checks that printed only command structure: the verbs applied to outside paths in each flagged call (ls, find, cd and echo only), a search of flagged commands for content-reading verbs (only 'head' trimming listings, one open() of the trial's own mirror, and 760485's own-folder steps), and a scan of every trial's Bash commands for git or bd invocations with quoted text removed (none).
_review.git_or_bd_flags: transcripts.py's git_or_bd flag marks 7 trials (154481, 5d36df, 79c26e, 842149, 8e5f02, 8edf7d, e5f8c2). All are false positives: the commands mention .git in a find exclusion, an 'ls -d .git' check, or echo text. No trial ran git or bd.
_review.rule: Pre-registered: reading a file's contents outside the trial (other than system or library files) or any network request excludes; listings don't. No flagged trial read outside contents and none made a network request, so all 36 are kept. The sensitivity analysis drops all 36.
